summary: Session 5 of 8, mid-set: does putting BOTH the target and the capturer inside a container remove the capability risk the operator named on 2026-08-16 -- that a screen recorder is a facility for an AI-driven process to read whatever is on their display -- and what does it cost? MACHINE VERDICT: PASS. Six scored criteria (I1-I6) plus I7 on presence of its required fields, three clean runs, and a fourth run interrupted while capture was OBSERVED producing bytes, excluded from the clean count. Criteria were committed BEFORE the first container run, the harness refuses to run without them and stamps their SHA-256 into every measurement, and the verdict is computed by a separate script that reads the criteria and can produce no measurement of its own -- it refuses to score at all if the stamped digest no longer matches the file. I1 IS THE SESSION. A magenta window was raised and held FOREGROUND on the operator's real desktop for the whole of each container capture: host-pixel fraction in the recordings 0.000000, with the detector proved to fire first at 0.999746 through the identical pipeline. Isolation is also asserted STRUCTURALLY -- the harness builds the run argv and asserts no --privileged, no host net/ipc/pid/userns, no mount of /tmp/.X11-unix, /run/user, /dev/dri, /dev/snd or /dev/video0, and no forbidden env names -- and ZERO bind mounts are used at all, because a bind mount is a hole in the boundary under test; artifacts come out with podman cp afterwards. THE CHEAP MITIGATION DOES NOT DOMINATE, measured first as the spec ordered. OBS's --only-bundled-plugins removes exactly ONE module of twenty-five. What survives is the finding: 24 bundled modules totalling 317 MB including an embedded Chromium (obs-browser/CEF), the DirectShow camera path, the DeckLink SDK, NVIDIA filters, a VST host and a scriptable remote-control server. Every large dependency the Session 4 reservation worried about SHIPS WITH OBS, so a flag that skips non-bundled plugins cannot touch any of them. Both denominators are reported rather than the flattering one: 4% by module count, larger by bytes, so the flag removes the biggest single FILE and none of the biggest RISKS. OBS WAS RUN IN THE CONTAINER, not substituted away. It starts under Mesa software rendering with no GPU device passed in, loads a seeded profile and scene collection, and records -- headless OBS in a container is feasible, which nobody here knew this morning. It did NOT produce a clean capture of the target: with no window manager, --minimize-to-tray has no tray, so OBS renders its GUI onto the display it captures (the first run came out 27% magenta and ~70% OBS), and obs_main_window_mapped is 1 on every run even after unmapping. The scored path is therefore ffmpeg x11grab, and OBS is recorded as feasible-and-unfinished with window suppression as the named next problem -- not as an unexplained instrument mystery, which is a claim this session made and then withdrew on evidence. THE FIDELITY TRADE, named from the runs: the captured window is titled 'Welcome - fixture - Visual Studio Code' on a bare X display with no window manager, so no title-bar controls, no Windows chrome, Linux fonts. The container is the right home for VERIFICATION capture and the wrong home for TRAINING capture, which is exactly the split the operator ruled the same day when they put Sessions 7 and 8 on the host. Endorsed on evidence rather than deference. COST: 1,900 MB image, 56.1 s cold build (--no-cache; `podman rmi` alone keeps the layer cache and reported 2.9 s, which would have shipped as a cold number), 1.9 s warm, 24.4 s container cold start, 12 s capture. --cap-drop=ALL BREAKS THE TARGET, measured: 2 VS Code processes and 0 mapped windows with it, 15 and 4 without, because Chromium's sandbox needs capabilities to build its user namespace. Keeping the flag and passing --no-sandbox was REFUSED -- unsandboxing a browser engine to satisfy a flag is the convenience this session exists to reject -- so the residual is stated: the container runs with Podman's default capability set, plus --network=none and --security-opt=no-new-privileges. The security POLICY is lifted from ai_router/podman_sandbox.py; the plumbing is not, because run_probe_in_container mounts the repo at /repo and a capture container must have no repo mount at all. FIVE VERIFICATION ROUNDS FOUND EIGHT DISTINCT MAJORS, every one accepted, none disputed. The pattern in them is worth more than the list: nearly every finding was this session ASSERTING something instead of OBSERVING it. Three were false passes in this session's own verdict script -- I5 certified the set's cardinal degradation guarantee by scoring three bare podman commands, I6 claimed deterministic cleanup having induced no failure and inspected no files, and I7's required fields were copied rather than checked. Round 2 caught the worst: the plugin probe launched THE OPERATOR'S LIVE OBS CONFIGURATION, which Session 4 had already recorded as carrying a webcam, a microphone and Desktop Audio -- a probe written to measure recorder risk could have initialised the operator's camera to do it. Round 3 rejected two of my fixes for testing themselves: the degradation test called a private helper that always reported success while the documented command aborted with no manifest, and the 'mid-run' failure fired AFTER capture, copying and analysis had all succeeded and was still counted as one of three clean runs. Round 4 rejected the next attempt because the interruption trusted a fixed 22-second timer to mean 'capture is active' against a measurement recording 24.5 s of startup, and because the failure run never raised the headed marker. Round 5 accepted six fixes and found one more: stopping podman-machine-default is a SHARED-RESOURCE side effect that can strand an operator's unrelated containers while the harness publishes 'machine left in entry state' from a VM status string. EACH FIX REPLACED AN ASSUMPTION WITH AN OBSERVATION: a growing capture file polled inside the container, a browser reporting its own disconnection, OBS's log naming the sources it initialised, a --no-cache build rather than a tag deletion, a container inventory compared across the machine stop rather than a status string, and a refusal to stop the machine at all when anything not owned by this harness is running. TWO INSTRUMENT DEFECTS THIS SESSION FOUND IN ITSELF are kept in the record because each produced a clean-looking result worth nothing: the positive control FAILED OPEN -- xsetroot returned exit 0 and captured an all-black screen, because the X server resets when its last client disconnects -- and a fact parser silently dropped host_x11_socket_present, the fact I4 most needs, because its regex could not match digits. The verdict now requires each I4 fact to be OBSERVED rather than merely un-contradicted. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated rather than left to be assumed: the extension is INSTALLED and VS Code runs with it, which is not activation and not rendering -- nobody has looked at the Work Explorer's tree under software rendering. Nothing about Windows display scaling (a virtual display has one fixed geometry, and I3 deliberately dropped Session 4's scaling claim). Nothing about tutorial-length recordings: runs are 12 seconds. And no first-build cost on a clean machine, since no registry pull was measured. SUITES: pytest 4986 passed / 5 skipped / 1 xfailed, mocha 1548 passed, Layer 3 37 passed, all recorded after the last change. ONE ITEM IS OPEN AND IT IS THE OPERATOR'S. Rounds 4 and 5 ran on their explicit authorization of 'up to two more', and that is spent. Round 5's finding is REMEDIATED BUT UNREVIEWED: no verifier has judged the refusal-based fix to the shared-machine hazard. The loop is SUSPENDED and this session does not have the authority to settle it -- self-authorizing another round is precisely what the bound exists to prevent. Accept, dismiss, or authorize one more round.

blockers.what: Round 5's Major is remediated but UNREVIEWED, and the verification loop is suspended.
blockers.detail: The documented measurement command stopped the shared podman-machine-default unconditionally and reported restoration from a VM status string that knows nothing about what was running inside it. Fixed by refusing to stop the machine when any container not owned by this harness is running, and by comparing the container INVENTORY across the stop. No verifier has judged that fix: rounds 4 and 5 consumed the operator's authorization of 'up to two more', and the bounded loop refuses a further cycle on this session's own authority.

residuals: OBS in the container is feasible and unfinished: it runs, renders in software and records, but its own window stays mapped on the display it captures (obs_main_window_mapped: 1 on every run), so no clean OBS capture of the target was obtained. Window suppression is the named next problem.
The Dabbler extension is installed and VS Code runs with it; activation and Work Explorer RENDERING under Linux software rendering are unobserved and unmeasured.
The container runs with Podman's default capability set. --cap-drop=ALL was measured to break Chromium's sandbox and the --no-sandbox workaround was refused.
No first-build cost on a clean machine: the cold build is --no-cache but the base image was already local, so no registry pull is included.
Runs are 12 seconds. A tutorial-length capture inside a container is unmeasured.
s5-obs-container-measurement.json is retained as raw OBS evidence in a SUPERSEDED shape; its stale fields are named inside the file itself and it is never scored.

What it cannot claim is that anybody looked. The guided look is written and offered; whether to spend ten minutes on it is the operator's decision.
